title: Conjecture on the construction code maximizing Kemeny's constant for threshold graphs
statement: Let $G$ be a threshold graph of order $n$, represented by a construction code, and let $\mathcal{K}(G)$ denote its Kemeny constant. **Maximizing construction-code conjecture.** The threshold graph of order $n$ with maximum Kemeny's constant has construction code of the form $0111..1100000...0001$. This conjecture has been confirmed computationally for all threshold graphs of orders up to $n=30$, but the asserted form is not established in general.
source_name: Jane Breen, Sooyeong Kim, Alexander Low Fung, Amy Mann, Andrei A. Parfeni and Giovanni Tedesco, “Threshold graphs, Kemeny's constant, and related random walk parameters”, arXiv:2310.08552 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08552

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

title: Erdős' existence conjecture for high-girth Steiner triple systems
statement: A **Steiner system** with parameters $(n,q,r)$ is a design with parameters $(n,q,r,1)$. In a partial $(n,q,r)$-Steiner system, a **$(j,i)$-configuration** is a set of $i$ $q$-element subsets spanning at most $j$ vertices, and the **girth** is the smallest integer $g\geq2$ for which the system has a $((q-r)g+r,g)$-configuration. **Erdős' high-girth conjecture.** For every integer $g\geq2$, there exists $n_g$ such that for all $n \geq n_g$ with $n\equiv 1,3 \mod 6$, there exists an $(n,3,2)$-Steiner system with girth at least $g$. This conjecture was stated by Erdős in 1973 and, according to the source, was proved in full by Kwan, Sah, Sawhney, and Simkin in 2022; approximate versions and earlier partial results preceded that resolution.
source_name: Michelle Delcourt and Luke Postle, “Proof of the High Girth Existence Conjecture via Refined Absorption”, arXiv:2402.17856 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17856

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of February 2024); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

title: The initial log-concavity thresholds for k-th power partition functions
statement:
For an integer $k\geq 2$, let $p^k(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ into perfect $k$-th powers. Define $N_k$ to be the smallest index such that the sequence $\{p^k(n)\}$ is log-concave for all $n>N_k$.

**Initial log-concavity threshold conjecture.** For $k\leq6$, the smallest such values are

$$
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
p^k(n)&p^2(n)&p^3(n)&p^4(n)&p^5(n)&p^6(n)\\
\hline
N_k&1041&15655&637854&2507860&35577568
\end{array}
$$

These values record the first index after which log-concavity is observed for the square through sixth-power partition functions. The source gives no proof or resolution of this finite-data assertion.
source_name: Arindam Roy, “Log-concavity And The Multiplicative Properties of Restricted Partition Functions”, arXiv:2404.03153 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.03153

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

title: Stabilization conjecture for log-concavity of k-regular partitions
statement:
Let $p_k(n)$ denote the number of $k$-regular partitions of $n$, and let $N_k$ be the smallest integer such that the sequence $\\{p_k(n)\\}_n$ is log-concave at every $n\geq N_k$. Write $N_{\infty}=26$, the corresponding threshold for the partition function.

**Log-concavity stabilization conjecture.** Let $k\geq 2$. Then

$$
N_k=N_{\infty}
$$

if $k\geq 30$.

The conjecture asserts that, for sufficiently large $k$, the exceptions to log-concavity of the $k$-regular partition function stabilize and coincide with those for the ordinary partition function. The source reports computational evidence for $2\leq k\leq 100$ and notes that the case $k=2$ was subsequently proved by Dong and Ji; the stated assertion for all $k\geq 30$ remains open in the supplied text.
source_name: Bernhard Heim and Markus Neuhauser, “Inequalities for k-regular partitions”, arXiv:2406.10987 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10987

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

title: Jedwab–Pender conjecture on even-length quaternary Legendre pairs
statement:
A **quaternary Legendre pair** is a pair of quaternary sequences satisfying the Legendre-pair correlation conditions; here the length is an even integer $2N$.

**Jedwab–Pender conjecture.** There exists a quaternary Legendre pair of even length $2N$ for every $N\geq 1$.

Quaternary Legendre pairs generalize binary Legendre pairs and can be used to construct quaternary Hadamard matrices. Before this paper, the smallest open case of the conjecture was length $36$; the paper gives general constructions of even lengths but the universal assertion remains open in the supplied text.
source_name: Jonathan Jedwab and Thomas Pender, “Two constructions of quaternary Legendre pairs of even length”, arXiv:2408.08472 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.08472

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2024).

title: The ballot-property conjecture for stable configurations on undirected binary trees
statement:
Let a **stable configuration** be a chip distribution on an undirected binary tree, and say that it satisfies the **ballot property** if, for each $i\in\mathbb{N}$, the $i$th smallest chip in the subtree rooted at the left child of a subtree's root has a smaller label than the $i$th smallest chip in the subtree rooted at the right child. A subtree means any subtree of the tree.

**Ballot-property conjecture.** In a stable configuration, the whole tree and every subtree satisfy the ballot property.

The paper establishes the property for subtrees with two or three layers and reports computational verification for every stable configuration starting with $15$ chips. The general assertion remains unresolved in the supplied text.
source_name: Ryota Inagaki, Tanya Khovanova and Austin Luo, “On Chip-Firing on Undirected Binary Trees”, arXiv:2410.00039 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00039

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

title: Maximum preimage conjecture for the $1\underline{23}$ and $3\underline{21}$ stack-sorting maps
statement:
Let $\mathfrak S_n$ be the set of permutations of length $n$, and let $\text{SC}_{1\underline{23}}$ and $\text{SC}_{3\underline{21}}$ be the corresponding vincular-pattern-avoiding stack-sorting maps. **Maximum-preimage conjecture.** For every $n\ge 2$,

$$
\max_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_n}|\text{SC}_{1\underline{23}}^{-1}(\pi)|=\max_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_n}|\text{SC}_{3\underline{21}}^{-1}(\pi)|=2^{n-2}.
$$

The claim gives the maximum possible preimage count for both maps. The surrounding paper develops bounds and related constructions, but the supplied text does not state a resolution of this assertion.
source_name: William Zhao, “Stack-sorting with Stacks Avoiding Vincular Patterns”, arXiv:2410.17057 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17057

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

title: The periodic characterization of the greedy 3-subsumfree sequence S_{1,2,3}
statement:
Let $S_{1,2,3}$ be the greedy 3-subsumfree sequence beginning with $1,2,3$: after the initial values, each term is the smallest larger integer that is not the sum of three distinct previous terms. **The periodic characterization conjecture.** For every positive integer $z$,

$$
z\in S_{1,2,3}\quad\iff\quad z\in\{1,5,13\}\ \text{or}\ z\bmod 23\in\{2,3,4,14,15\}.
$$

The paper reports that Walnut verifies this statement, so it is subsequently promoted to a theorem.
source_name: Wieb Bosma, Rene Bruin, Robbert Fokkink, Jonathan Grube, Anniek Reuijl and Thian Tromp, “Using Walnut to solve problems from the OEIS”, arXiv:2503.04122 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.04122

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of March 2025); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

title: The generalized periodic characterization conjecture for S_{1,g,g+1}
statement:
For $g\geq 2$, let $S_{1,g,g+1}$ be the greedy 3-subsumfree sequence beginning with $1,g,g+1$, where each subsequent term is the smallest larger integer that is not the sum of three distinct previous terms. **The generalized periodic characterization conjecture.** For every $g\geq2$,

$$
z\in S_{1,g,g+1}\iff z\in\{1,2g+1,6g+1\}\ \text{or}\ z\bmod(10g+3)\in\{g,g+1,\ldots,2g\}\cup\{6g+2,6g+3,\ldots,7g+1\}.
$$

In particular, after the first $g+4$ entries, the sequence modulo $10g+3$ is periodic with period $2g+1$. The paper reports verification only for $g\in\{2,3,\ldots,10\}$ and leaves the parametrized statement conjectural.
source_name: Wieb Bosma, Rene Bruin, Robbert Fokkink, Jonathan Grube, Anniek Reuijl and Thian Tromp, “Using Walnut to solve problems from the OEIS”, arXiv:2503.04122 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.04122

title: Bounded treedepth for even-cycle-subgraph-free graphs of diameter three
statement:
Let $r\geq 4$. A graph is **$C_{2r}$-subgraph-free** if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to the cycle $C_{2r}$. The diameter of a graph is the maximum distance between two vertices. **The even-cycle treedepth conjecture.** For every $r\geq 4$, the class of $C_{2r}$-subgraph-free graphs of diameter at most $3$ has bounded treedepth.

The conjecture would complete the classification of bounded treedepth for even-cycle-subgraph-free graphs of diameter three. Boundedness is established for $r=4$ by an involved case analysis and for $r\in\{5,\ldots,12\}$ with computer assistance, while the general case remains open.
source_name: Konrad K. Dabrowski, Tala Eagling-Vose, Noleen Köhler, Sebastian Ordyniak and Daniël Paulusma, “Bounding Width on Graph Classes of Constant Diameter”, arXiv:2505.19926 (2025).

title: Uniqueness of the centroid-preserving triangle center for arbitrary quadrilaterals
statement:
Let $ABCD$ be an arbitrary quadrilateral, and let $X$ be a triangle center. Let $E$, $F$, $G$, and $H$ be the $X$-points of $\triangle BCD$, $\triangle CDA$, $\triangle DAB$, and $\triangle ABC$, respectively.

**Centroid-preservation uniqueness conjecture.** The centroid of $ABCD$ coincides with the centroid of $EFGH$ if and only if $X=X_2$.

This is posed as an example in a request to determine whether a relationship found by searching the first 1000 centers is unique or whether further centers satisfy it. The source provides no proof or resolution.
source_name: Stanley Rabinowitz and Ercole Suppa, “More Relationships between a Central Quadrilateral and its Reference Quadrilateral”, arXiv:2506.17240 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.17240

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2025).

title: Liechti–Strenner's minimal dilatation conjecture for closed nonorientable surfaces
statement:
Let $N_g$ be the closed nonorientable surface of genus $g$, and let $[+]{\delta}^{+}(N_g)$ denote the minimal dilatation among pseudo-Anosov diffeomorphisms of $N_g$ with an orientable invariant foliation. For each integer $k\geq 2$, let $r_k$ be the largest real root of

$$
x^{2k-1}-x^k-x^{k-1}-1.
$$

**Liechti–Strenner's conjecture.** For all $k\geq 2$,

$$
\delta^{+}(N_{2k})=r_k.
$$

Liechti and Strenner determined this minimal dilatation for several even genera, including $4,6,8,10,12,14,16,20,24,28,32,36$ and $40$; the conjecture predicts the formula for every even genus at least $4$.
source_name: Ji-Young Ham and Joongul Lee, “Maximal dilatation on nonorientable surfaces”, arXiv:2508.08323 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.08323

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2025).

title: Conjecture on fractional domatic number of planar graphs by girth
statement:
For an integer $g\ge 3$, let $\mathcal{P}_g$ be the class of planar graphs $G$ with minimum degree $\delta(G)=2$ and girth at least $g$. Write

$$
\operatorname{FDOM}(\mathcal{P}_g)=\inf\{\operatorname{FDOM}(G):G\in\mathcal{P}_g\}.
$$

**Planar girth fractional-domatic conjecture.** For every integer $k\ge 1$, if $3k-1\le g\le 3k+1$, then

$$
\operatorname{FDOM}(\mathcal{P}_g)=\frac{3k+1}{k+1}.
$$

The value is known to be $2$ for $g\le 4$, $7/3$ for $5\le g\le 7$, and $5/2$ for $8\le g\le 10$. The conjecture predicts the general extremal value, suggested by cycles, and remains open beyond these established ranges.
source_name: Quentin Chuet, Hugo Demaret, Hoang La and François Pirot, “Fractional domatic number and minimum degree”, arXiv:2508.19617 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.19617

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2025).

title: Kaiser's lower-bound conjecture for three perfect matchings
statement:
Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph, and let $m_3(G)$ be the ratio of the maximum number of edges covered by the union of three perfect matchings to $|E(G)|$.

**Kaiser's conjecture.** For every bridgeless cubic graph $G$,

$$
m_3(G)\geq \frac45.
$$

Kaiser et al. proved the weaker bound $m_3(G)\geq 27/35\approx 0.77$ and conjectured that $4/5$ is the best possible lower bound, attained by the Petersen graph.
source_name: Edita Máčajová and Ján Mazák, “On covering cubic graphs with three perfect matchings”, arXiv:2509.05501 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.05501

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2025).

title: Extremal lower bound for the suspended 6-cycle
statement:
Let $C_6$ be the $6$-cycle, let $C_6(t)$ denote the associated $3$-uniform hypergraph obtained by adjoining a new vertex to every edge of $C_6$, and let $\operatorname{ex}(n,H)$ denote the $n$-vertex extremal number of $H$. **Extremal lower-bound conjecture for $C_6(t)$.** There is a constant $C>0$ such that, for all $t\geq C$,

$$
\operatorname{ex}(n,C_6(t))\geq\Omega\left(n^{17/6}\right).
$$

The paper identifies this as one of the smallest interesting unknown cases of the preceding KST-type conjecture; the matching upper bound is known from its main extremal theorem because $C_6$ is Sidorenko.
source_name: Hyunwoo Lee, “On Sidorenko exponents of hypergraphs”, arXiv:2509.08680 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.08680

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2025).

title: Numerical threshold conjecture for cubic overpartition Jensen polynomials
statement:
Let $\overline{a}(n)$ denote the cubic overpartition function, and define its Jensen polynomials by

$$
J_{\overline{a}}^{d,n}(X):=\sum_{i=0}^{d}\binom{d}{i}\overline{a}(n+i)X^i.
$$

For each degree $d$, let $N_{\overline{a}}(d)$ be the minimum integer such that $J_{\overline{a}}^{d,n-1}(X)$ is hyperbolic for all $n\geq N_{\overline{a}}(d)$. **The numerical threshold conjecture.** The observed threshold values are

$$
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
d&3&4&5&6&7\\hline
N_{\overline{a}}(d)&39&89&172&279&423
\end{array}
$$

These values are based on numerical evidence from Mathematica; the source does not provide a proof or resolution of the conjecture.
source_name: Archit Agarwal, Meghali Garg and Bibekananda Maji, “Rademacher-type exact formula and higher order Turán inequalities for cubic overpartitions”, arXiv:2509.23151 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23151

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2025). “This conjecture was settled by Griffin, Ono, Rolen and Zagier .”

title: Uniform better-than-square-root cancellation conjecture for smooth numbers
statement:
Let $f$ be a Steinhaus random multiplicative function, let $P(n)$ denote the largest prime factor of $n$, and define

$$
\Psi(x,y)=\#\{n\leqslant x:P(n)\leqslant y\}.
$$

**Uniform smooth-number cancellation conjecture.** The paper conjectures that its main estimate should hold uniformly for every $2\leqslant y\leqslant x$:

$$
\mathbb E\left|\sum_{\substack{1\leqslant n\leqslant x\\P(n)\leqslant y}}f(n)\right|=o\left(\Psi(x,y)^{1/2}\right).
$$

The proved theorem establishes this only for $(\log x)^{30}\leqslant y\leqslant x$; extending it to the full range $2\leqslant y\leqslant x$ remains open.
source_name: Seth Hardy and Max Wenqiang Xu, “Helson's conjecture for smooth numbers”, arXiv:2511.03430 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.03430

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2025).

title: The extremal solvabilizer conjecture for finite groups
statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, and define

$$
\operatorname{Solv}(G)=\{\operatorname{Sol}_G(x):x\in G\}.
$$

A composition factor of $G$ is a factor in a composition series of $G$.

**Extremal solvabilizer conjecture.** If

$$
|\operatorname{Solv}(G)|=32,
$$

then $G$ has a composition factor isomorphic to $A_5$.

The preceding theorem establishes the lower bound $|\operatorname{Solv}(G)|\geq 32$ for every nonsolvable finite group. Thus the conjecture concerns the equality case and asserts that the smallest possible nonsolvable value is explained by the occurrence of $A_5$ as a composition factor.
source_name: Banafsheh Akbari, Ethan Han, Sasha Lin and Benjamin Vakil, “The Number of Solvabilizers in Finite Groups”, arXiv:2511.11544 (2025).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2024–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2403.08129](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.08129).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.11544

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).

title: Half-induced-forest conjecture for graphs on surfaces
statement:
For a graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and genus $g$, let $\alpha_1(G)$ denote the order of a largest induced $1$-degenerate subgraph of $G$, equivalently a largest induced forest. **Half-induced-forest conjecture.** For every non-negative integer $g$, there exists a constant $f(g)$ such that every graph $G$ of genus $g$ satisfies

$$
\alpha_1(G)\geq \frac{n}{2}-f(g).
$$

The conjecture is known for triangle-free planar graphs, where the source cites the stronger bound $\alpha_1(G)\geq (6n+7)/11$. It remains open for graphs on surfaces in general.
source_name: Alexander Clow, Sean Kim and Ladislav Stacho, “A Note on Large Degenerate Induced Subgraphs in Sparse Graphs”, arXiv:2511.13693 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.13693

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).

title: Order-7 spiral optimality conjecture for fixed vertex number
statement:
For a given positive integer $n$, let $e_d(n)$ be the maximum number of edges among penny graphs with $n$ vertices and distance $d$, and let $d(7)$ be the distance associated with the order-$7$ triangular tiling. **Order-7 spiral optimality conjecture.** Among all $d>0$, a spiral with $n$ vertices of the order-$7$ triangular tiling has the maximum number of edges; equivalently, 
$$
\max_{d>0} e_d(n)=e_{d(7)}(n).
$$
 The proposition stated after this conjecture verifies it for all $n\leq 366536$ and for $n=7F_{2k+1}-6$, $k\geq 0$, where $F_i$ is the $i$th Fibonacci number; the general assertion remains open.
source_name: Ádám Sagmeister and Konrad J. Swanepoel, “Penny graphs in the hyperbolic plane”, arXiv:2512.24832 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24832

title: The exact L(3,2,1)-labeling number of odd 4-valent circulants with steps 1 and 5
statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ be odd with $n\geq105$, and let $G=C_n(\\{1,5,n-5,n-1\\})$. The invariant $\lambda_{(3,2,1)}(G)$ is the minimum span of an $L(3,2,1)$-labeling of $G$, meaning a labeling of the vertices by nonnegative integers such that labels of vertices at distances $1$, $2$, and $3$ differ by at least $3$, $2$, and $1$, respectively.

**Exact labeling-number conjecture.**

$$
\lambda_{(3,2,1)}(G)=14.
$$

The source constructs an $L(3,2,1)$-labeling with span $14$ for the stated range, while computer tests found no labeling with labels $0,1,\ldots,13$ for odd $n\leq101$. Thus the conjecture combines the construction with the expected lower bound for all odd $n\geq105$.
source_name: Přemysl Holub and Martin Kopřiva, “L(3,2,1)-labelings of three classes of 4-valent circulants”, arXiv:2601.12574 (2026).

title: Wojda's conjecture on packing digraphs
statement:
Let $D$ and $D'$ be digraphs, and let $|A(D)|$ denote the size of $D$, meaning its number of arcs. For every integer $n$ and every $m$ satisfying

$$
2\leq m\leq \frac{n}{2},
$$

write $\mu(n,k)$ for the smallest number such that there exist digraphs $D$ and $D'$ of order $n$, with $|A(D)|=k$ and $|A(D')|=\mu(n,k)$, that do not pack. **Wojda's conjecture.** For every $m$ satisfying $2\leq m\leq \frac{n}{2}$,

$$
\mu(n,n-m)=2n-\left\lfloor\frac{n}{m}\right\rfloor.
$$

Equivalently, the condition that one digraph has size at most $n-m$ and the other has size less than $2n-\lfloor n/m\rfloor$ guarantees that the two digraphs pack. The paper confirms the conjecture for $m\geq 93$ and $n\geq 31m$; the general statement remains open.
source_name: Maciej Cisiński and Andrzej Żak, “Further progress on Wojda's conjecture”, arXiv:2601.13085 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.13085

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2026).

title: Rich flow number conjecture
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $\Delta$. A **rich $k$-flow** is a nowhere-zero $k$-flow $\phi$ such that $|\phi(e)|\neq |\phi(f)|$ for every pair of adjacent edges $e$ and $f$. The graph $G$ is **rich flow admissible** if it is bridgeless and no two edges forming a $2$-edge-cut are incident with a common vertex.

**Rich flow number conjecture.** If $\Delta\geq 5$, then $G$ admits a rich $\lfloor 1.5\Delta+1\rfloor$-flow.

The paper proves a linear upper bound of $(264\Delta-521)$ for rich flow admissible graphs. The conjectured bound is motivated by examples whose rich flow number is $3k+1$ when the maximum degree is $2k$, and remains open.
source_name: Robert Lukoťka, “A Linear Bound on the Rich Flow Number for Graphs with a Given Maximum Degree”, arXiv:2601.16104 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.16104

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2026).

title: Positivity conjecture for cumulants of minimum matching costs
statement:
Let $C_{k,m,n}$ be the minimum cost of a $k$-matching in the random bipartite matching model, and let its cumulants $\kappa_p$ be defined by

$$
\log F_{k,m,n}(t)=\sum_{p=1}^{\infty}\frac{\kappa_p t^p}{p!},
$$

where $F_{k,m,n}(t)=\mathbb{E}(\exp(t\cdot C_{k,m,n}))$ is the moment generating function. **Positivity conjecture.** All the cumulants of $C_{k,m,n}$ are positive.
This conjecture is based on computations for all $k\leq m\leq n\leq 15$ and less systematic computations for larger parameters; no proof or disproof is given in the source.
source_name: Johan Wästlund, “Moment generating functions in combinatorial optimization: Bipartite matching”, arXiv:2602.07563 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07563

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2026).

title: The recursive bound for tone chromatic numbers of subcubic outerplanar graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a subcubic outerplanar graph, meaning that $G$ is outerplanar and has maximum degree at most $3$. For each positive integer $t$, let $\tau_t(G)$ denote the smallest number of colors in a $t$-tone coloring of $G$. **The recursive bound.** For every integer $t\ge 3$,

$$
\tau_t(G)\le \tau_{t-1}(G)+t+1.
$$

This is proposed as a relationship between successive tone chromatic numbers after the paper establishes the sharp bound $\tau_3(G)\le 11$ for subcubic outerplanar graphs. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
source_name: Hadeel Al Bazzal and Olivier Togni, “t-tone colorings of outerplanar and Halin graphs”, arXiv:2603.18674 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.18674

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of March 2026). “In , Cranston, Kim, and Kinnersley confirmed the first part of the conjecture and disproved the third by presenting a counterexample, namely the Heawood graph, which does not contain $K_4-e$.”

title: Universal odd critical exponent conjecture for exponential-kernel minimizers
statement:
Consider the minimum-energy problem for $k$ points on the unit interval with pairwise kernel $e^{-|x-y|^q}$, and write an odd number of points as

$$
k=2m+1.
$$

Let the global critical exponent be the value of $q$ at which the globally minimizing configuration changes phase, and let the universal odd value be the value given by equation. **Universal odd critical exponent conjecture.** For every odd $k=2m+1$, the true global critical exponent equals the universal odd value in equation. The conjecture is motivated by the explicit branch crossing and numerical evidence for $k=3,5,7,9,11,13,15,19$; the unresolved issue is excluding a lower-energy competing branch with more than one interior point.
source_name: Michael T. M. Emmerich, “Critical phase transitions in minimum-energy configurations for the exponential kernel family e^-|x-y|^q on the unit interval”, arXiv:2603.28179 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28179

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).

title: The exact minimum percolating-set size conjecture for 4-neighbour bootstrap percolation on hypercubes
statement:
Let $Q_d$ be the $d$-dimensional hypercube, and let $m(Q_d;4)$ denote the minimum cardinality of a set that percolates under the $4$-neighbour bootstrap process on $Q_d$. **Exact-size conjecture.** For all $d\geq4$ with $d\neq5$,

$$
m(Q_d;4)=\left\lceil\frac{d(d^2+3d+14)}{24}\right\rceil+1.
$$

The paper states that this would extend the main theorem to all $d\geq4$ except $d=5$, which was ruled out by exhaustive computer search; the claim is presented as a conjectural extension because the authors have proved it only for some values of $d$.
source_name: Jonathan A. Noel, “Optimal and Near-Optimal Constructions for Bootstrap Percolation in Hypercubes”, arXiv:2604.15534 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15534

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2026).

title: The induced $P_6$ planar Turán number conjecture
statement:
Let $P_6$ be the path on six vertices, and let ${\mathrm{ex}}_{\mathcal P}(n,P_6^{\mathrm{ind}})$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex planar graph containing no induced copy of $P_6$. **The induced $P_6$ planar Turán number conjecture.** For every $n\geq 3$,

$$
{\mathrm{ex}}_{\mathcal P}(n,P_6^{\mathrm{ind}})=\begin{cases}3n-6,& n\leq 19,\\ \left\lfloor\frac{50}{17}(n-2)\right\rfloor+1,& n\geq 20.
\end{cases}
$$

This is presented as a conjecture for the more challenging problem of forbidding induced paths $P_k$ for $k\geq 6$; the claimed exact values remain open.
source_name: Ervin Győri and Hilal Hama Karim, “Induced planar Turán numbers”, arXiv:2604.25829 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.25829

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2026). “The full characterization of graphs $F$ for which $\ex_\cP(n, F^\ind) = 3n-6$ remains an interesting open question.”

title: Quadratic polynomial primitive-divisor density conjecture
statement:
Let $\phi\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ be quadratic, with infinite critical orbit and all iterates irreducible. For an integer sequence $a_n=\phi(a_{n-1})$, let $P(a_n)$ denote the largest prime factor of $a_n$, and let $D$ denote the associated natural density. **Quadratic polynomial primitive-divisor density conjecture.** For every $a_0\in\mathbb{Z}$,

$$
D(P(a_n))=0.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by computations and heuristics and is also identified as Conjecture 5.7 of [13]; no resolution is given in the source.
source_name: Rafe Jones, “2007: An Arboreal Odyssey: A View of Arboreal Galois Representations and Applications, from Early in the Subject's History”, arXiv:2605.21666 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21666

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2026).

title: The diagonal maximal-covering-number conjecture for cross-intersecting families
statement:
Let $m(k,k)$ denote the maximum product of the sizes of two cross-intersecting families with maximal covering number $k$ in the setting of the paper. **The diagonal conjecture.** For all $k\geq 2$, 

$$
m(k,k)=(k^{k-1}+k-1)^2.
$$

The authors note that this agrees with the proved cases $m(2,2)=3^2$ and $m(3,3)=11^2$, and with the construction giving the bound for large values of $k$; the assertion remains open in general.
source_name: Long Lin, Peter Frankl and Hehui Wu, “On the product of cross-intersecting families with maximal covering number”, arXiv:2606.01817 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.01817

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).

title: Planar D-chromatic index conjecture
statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph with maximum degree $\Delta\ge 4$, and let $\chi'_D(G)$ denote the minimum number of colors in a proper edge coloring in which every diamond subgraph is rainbow.

**Planar D-chromatic index conjecture.** For every such graph,

$$
\chi'_D(G)\le\begin{cases} 9 &\text{if } \Delta=4, \\ 10 &\text{if } \Delta=5, \\ 2\Delta-1 &\text{if } \Delta\ge 6. \end{cases}
$$

This conjecture concerns the sharper planar bounds not established by the results stated in the provided text; the text gives the general planar bound $\chi'_D(G)\le 2\Delta$ for $\Delta\ge 38$.
source_name: Runze Wang, “Proper edge coloring with rainbow diamonds”, arXiv:2606.06831 (2026).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2022–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2208.13297](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.13297).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06831

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2026). “Regarding this conjecture, the first non-trivial case $\Delta=3$ has been verified by Andersen and by Hor\'ak et al. , but it is still open for $\Delta\ge 4$.”

title: Sharpness conjecture for the three-uniform Erdős–Frankl–Pach bound
statement:
Let $M_3(n)$ denote the maximum size of a family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\binom{[n]}{4}$ with $\operatorname{VC}(\mathcal{F})\le 3$. The paper establishes the lower bound

$$
M_3(n)\ge \binom{n-1}{3}+n-3
$$

for every $n\ge 6$. **Three-uniform sharpness conjecture.** For all sufficiently large $n$,

$$
M_3(n)=\binom{n-1}{3}+n-3.
$$

This is presented as a suspected sharp bound; the restriction to sufficiently large $n$ is necessary because $M_3(8)\ge45$ while the displayed expression equals $40$.
source_name: Tuan Tran and Zixiang Xu, “Beating the Ahlswede–Khachatrian bound for the Erdős–Frankl–Pach problem”, arXiv:2606.23469 (2026).
references:
**21 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2007–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2508.13724](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.13724), [arXiv:2506.01739](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.01739), [arXiv:2504.14389](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14389), [arXiv:2404.02322](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.02322), [arXiv:2402.05702](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.05702), [arXiv:2306.11362](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.11362), [arXiv:2211.16434](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.16434), [arXiv:2106.02129](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.02129), [arXiv:1902.03166](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.03166), [arXiv:1902.03881](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.03881), [arXiv:1811.03080](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.03080), [arXiv:1712.04438](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.04438), and 8 more.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23469

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2026). “Ahlswede and Khachatrian disproved this conjecture in 1997 by giving a family of size $\binom{n-1}{d}+\binom{n-4}{d-2}$.”

title: Dirac's 1-Factorization Conjecture
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of even order, and let $k$ be an integer. A graph is **1-factorable** if its edges can be partitioned into 1-factors, equivalently if its chromatic index equals its maximum degree. **1-Factorization Conjecture.** If $G$ is $k$-regular for some

$$
k\geq 2\left\lceil\frac{|V(G)|}{4}\right\rceil-1,
$$

then $G$ is 1-factorable; equivalently, $\chi'(G)=\Delta(G)$. The conjecture is a central dense-graph edge-coloring assertion and was verified for all sufficiently large graphs by Csaba, Kühn, Lo, Osthus, and Treglown in 2016; the supplied source does not state that the finite conjecture is completely resolved.
source_name: Guantao Chen, Jessica McDonald and Songling Shan, “Towards the Overfull Conjecture II”, arXiv:2607.02270 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.02270

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).

title: Li–Peng square-root booksize conjecture for Nosal graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be an $m$-edge graph with spectral radius $\rho(G)>\sqrt{m}$. Such a graph is called **Nosal**, and let $bk(G)$ denote the maximum number of triangles sharing a common edge in $G$.

**Li–Peng conjecture.** For every $m$-edge Nosal graph $G$,

$$
bk(G)=\Omega(\sqrt{m}).
$$

Nikiforov had previously shown the weaker bound $bk(G)>\frac{1}{12}\sqrt[4]{m}$. The conjecture was confirmed by Li, Liu and Zhang, who proved $bk(G)>\frac{1}{24}\sqrt{m}$ and showed that the order $\sqrt{m}$ is best possible.
source_name: Xinghui Zhao, Lihua You, Jing Zeng and Xiaoxue Zhang, “Two problems on booksize and triangular edges in Nosal graphs”, arXiv:2607.15071 (2026).
references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2025–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2601.10163](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.10163), [arXiv:2508.14366](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.14366).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15071

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2026). “The conjecture was recently confirmed by Li, Liu and Zhang .”

title: Sharpening of Szabó's conjecture for arithmetic-progression-intersection families
statement:
Let $t(N)$ be the largest $t$ for which there exist distinct sets $A_1,\dots,A_t\subseteq\\{1,\dots,N\\}$ such that $A_i\cap A_j$ is a nonempty arithmetic progression for all $i\ne j$. A construction gives

$$
t(N)\ge \binom{N}{2}+1+\left\lfloor\frac{N-1}{4}\right\rfloor.
$$

**Sharpening of Szabó's conjecture.** Equality holds in this lower bound for every $N\ge 1$, that is,

$$
t(N)=\binom{N}{2}+1+\left\lfloor\frac{N-1}{4}\right\rfloor.
$$

The claim is verified computationally for $N\le 12$ and would imply the strongest form of Szabó's bound, while the remaining obstruction is the kernel question concerning whether an extremal family has a common element.
source_name: Zhanfu Yang, “Exact values and exact upper bounds for families of integers with arithmetic progression intersections (Erdős Problem #272)”, arXiv:2607.23004 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23004

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).

title: The Neoplatonic conjecture for Euclidean realizations
statement:
A **6-net** is a simplicial triangulation of the $2$-sphere with maximum degree at most $6$. A net is **prime** if every $3$-cycle bounds a face. For a $6$-net $\sigma$, write $\Delta(\sigma)$ for its Euclidean realization, when it exists.

**Neoplatonic conjecture.** Any $6$-net $\sigma$ has a realization, unique up to isometry, as an undented Euclidean polyhedron $\Delta(\sigma)$ built from equilateral triangles of side length $1$.

The conjecture is motivated by computational experiments and by the proved existence results for all $6$-nets with at most $50$ vertices; uniqueness of the Euclidean realization is not established in the source.
source_name: Peter Doyle and Matthew Ellison, “Neoplatonic solids”, arXiv:2607.26363 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26363

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).

title: The smallest singular value conjecture for Gaussian matrix perturbations
statement:
Let $\widetilde{A}$ be an arbitrary square matrix in $\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$, and let $A$ be a Gaussian perturbation of $\widetilde{A}$ with variance $\sigma^2$. **Smallest singular value conjecture.** It should satisfy

$$
\Pr\left\{\|A^{-1}\|_2\geq x\right\}\leq\frac{\sqrt{n}}{x\sigma}.
$$

This would extend Edelman's sharp Gaussian-matrix bound from perturbations of the zero matrix to arbitrary centers; the paper proves the same estimate with constant $2.35$ instead of $1$.
source_name: Arvind Sankar, Daniel A. Spielman and Shang-Hua Teng, “Smoothed Analysis of the Condition Numbers and Growth Factors of Matrices”, arXiv:cs/0310022 (2005).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/0310022

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2003).

title: The orbit lattice conjecture for platycosms
statement:
A **platycosm** $P$ is a compact flat three-dimensional manifold. Its **orbit lattice bound** $R_0$ is the maximum of the covering radii of all orbit lattices for $P$, and $P$ has the **orbit lattice property** if its diameter equals $R_0$.

**Orbit lattice conjecture for platycosms.** All 10 platycosms have the orbit lattice property.

The orbit lattice bound gives a lower bound for the diameter of every platycosm; when an orbit lattice has a translatable Voronoi tiling, the bound is attained. The conjecture asserts that this equality holds for all 10 platycosms.
source_name: John Horton Conway and Juan Pablo Rossetti, “Describing the platycosms”, arXiv:math/0311476 (2003).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0311476

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2003).

title: Conference-construction maximal-parameter conjecture for complex Hadamard matrices
statement: Let $D$ be an arbitrary dephased, symmetric complex Hadamard matrix arising from the conference matrix construction, of order $N$. Apply Construction by repeatedly selecting suitable pairs of rows and corresponding columns and introducing one free parameter at each step; the construction can introduce at most $\frac{N}{2}-1$ parameters. **Conference-construction maximal-parameter conjecture.** Construction leads to Hadamard matrices after each step, and, for $N\geq 14$, the maximum number $\frac{N}{2}-1$ of parameters can be introduced. The conjecture concerns the sufficiency of the two suitability conditions and the attainment of the maximal parameter count in this construction; the source reports examples for $D_{10}$ and $D_{14}$ but no general proof.
source_name: Ferenc Szöllosi, “Parametrizing Complex Hadamard Matrices”, arXiv:math/0610297 (2007).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0610297

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2006).

title: Linear upper bound conjecture for the longest solvable board
statement:
For an odd integer $n\geq 3$, let $ML(n)$ be the maximum length of a solvable board of size $n$:

$$
ML(n):=\max_{A\in Sol_n}\{\operatorname{length} A\}.
$$

**Linear upper bound conjecture.** As $n\to\infty$, $ML(n)=O(n)$.

The construction preceding this conjecture gives solvable boards of length $3n$ for all odd $n\geq 11$, while the trivial general upper bound is $ML(n)\leq n^2$. The conjecture asserts that the maximal length grows only linearly with the board size.
source_name: Ary Shaviv, “Board games, random boards and long boards”, arXiv:2110.05416 (2021).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.05416

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

title: Total-lamination conjecture for neighborly box families
statement: Let $S=\{0,1,*\}$, and let $S^d$ be the set of length-$d$ strings over $S$. A family $F\subseteq S^d$ is a **$k$-neighborly total lamination** if it is $k$-neighborly and is a total lamination under the recursive coordinate-splitting definition given in the paper. Let $n(k,d)$ denote the maximum size of a $k$-neighborly family in $S^d$. **Total-lamination conjecture.** For every $1\leqslant k\leqslant d$, there exists a $k$-neighborly total lamination $F\subseteq S^d$ with $|F|=n(k,d)$. The conjecture is known for $k=1$, $k=d-1$, and $k=d$, and in all cases where the exact value of $n(k,d)$ is known except $n(6,8)=150$; it remains open in general.
source_name: Noga Alon, Jarosław Grytczuk, Andrzej P. Kisielewicz and Krzysztof Przesławski, “New bounds on the maximum number of neighborly boxes in R^d”, arXiv:2212.05133 (2023).

title: Strict inequality between the 13-crossing and 5-crossing numbers
statement:
Let $K$ be a knot, and let $c_n(K)$ denote its $n$-crossing number, the minimum number of $n$-fold crossings in a projection of $K$. **Strict inequality conjecture.** For all knots $K$ such that $c_5(K)\geq 2$, one has

$$
c_{13}(K)<c_5(K).
$$

This conjecture predicts that, except for knots with $c_5(K)<2$, the 13-crossing number is strictly smaller than the 5-crossing number. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied source material.
source_name: Nicholas Hagedorn, “Strict Inequalities for the n-crossing Number”, arXiv:2212.12330 (2022).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2021–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2105.10921](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.10921).

title: Distinct spectral radii for Type 5 digraphs
statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $5\leq n$, and let $r_k,s_k,t_k$ satisfy

$$
4\leq r_k\leq s_k\leq t_k<n,\qquad r_k+s_k+t_k=2n,
$$

for $k=1,2$, with $(r_1,s_1,t_1)\neq(r_2,s_2,t_2)$. For each $k$, let $\rho_k$ be the only real positive root of

$$
x^n-x^{n-r_k}-x^{n-s_k}-x^{n-t_k}-2.
$$

**Distinct-root conjecture.** One has $\rho_1\neq\rho_2$. This asserts that distinct admissible parameter triples determine distinct spectral radii for the corresponding Type $5$ digraphs. The claim was computationally verified for $5\leq n\leq 200$; the conjecture proposes that it holds for every $n\geq5$.
source_name: Diego Bravo, Florencia Cubría, Marcelo Fiori and Gustavo Rama, “Some families of digraphs determined by the complementarity spectrum”, arXiv:2403.10665 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10665

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

title: Extremality conjecture for symmetric Hales–Jewett thresholds
statement:
Let $t,r\geq 2$. Write $n_{\mathrm{sym}}(t,r)$ for the largest $n$ such that $[t]^n$ admits a line-free symmetric $r$-coloring, and let $\mathrm{HJ}(t,r)$ denote the least $n$ such that every $r$-coloring of $[t]^n$ contains a monochromatic combinatorial line. A line-free symmetric coloring is in particular line-free, so

$$
n_{\mathrm{sym}}(t,r)\leq \mathrm{HJ}(t,r)-1.
$$

**Extremality conjecture.** For all $t,r\geq 2$,

$$
n_{\mathrm{sym}}(t,r)=\mathrm{HJ}(t,r)-1.
$$

The conjecture asserts that the upper bound obtained by restricting to symmetric colorings is always attained. The cited constructions give $n_{\mathrm{sym}}(3,3)\geq 21$ and $n_{\mathrm{sym}}(4,2)\geq 13$, but the general equality remains open.
source_name: Younes Mouhib, “Lower Bounds for the Hales-Jewett Numbers via Symmetric and One-Weight Colorings”, arXiv:2606.22155 (2026).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2604.26592](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.26592).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22155

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).

title: Problem 5.6 — Find H1(Ig(k), Z) for all k≥ 2.
statement: Find H1(Ig(k), Z) for all k≥ 2. Generating sets for Ig. One diﬃculty in working with Ig is the complexity of its generating sets: any such set must have at least 1 3 [4g3−g] elements since Ig has abelian quotients of this rank (see [ Jo5], Corollary after Theorem 5). Compare this with Mod g, which can always be generated by 2 g + 1 Dehn twists (Humphries), or even by 2 elements (Wajnryb [ W a])! How does one keep track, for example, of the (at least) 1330 generators for I 10? How does one even give a usable naming scheme for working with these? Even worse, in Johnson’s proof of finite generation of Ig (see [ Jo2]), the given generating set has O(2g) elements. The following therefore seems fundamental; at the very least it seems that solving it will require us to understand the combinatorial topology underlying Ig in a deeper way than we now understand it.
source_name: Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics

title: Random Sampling and Approximation of MAX-CSP Problems — Theorem 16
statement: Let $r,n$ be positive integers, with $r$ fixed, and let $\\epsilon$ be a positive real. A MAX-$r$CSP instance consists of a set $F$ of $m$ distinct Boolean functions $f_1,\ldots,f_m$ on Boolean variables $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, each function involving only $r$ of the variables. Let $\operatorname{Max}(F)$ be the maximum number of functions in $F$ that can simultaneously be set to $1$ by a truth assignment. For a subset $Q$ of the variables, let $F_Q$ be the subset of functions in $F$ involving only variables in $Q$ (and their negations). There exists a positive integer $q\in O(\log(1/\epsilon)/\epsilon^4)$ such that, if $Q$ is a uniformly random subset of $\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}$ of cardinality $q$, then with probability at least $9/10$, $$\left|\frac{n^r}{q^r}\operatorname{Max}(F_Q)-\operatorname{Max}(F)\right|\leq \epsilon n^r.$$
source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2004/28, page 49
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2004/28](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/730), page 49. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Superlinear Circuit Lower Bounds for Explicit Boolean Functions
statement:
There exists a Boolean function family f_n:{0,1}^n->{0,1}, n>=1, evaluated by a single deterministic polynomial-time algorithm on (1^n,x), whose minimum gate count C_B2(f_n) over single-output fan-in-two circuits using arbitrary binary Boolean gates satisfies C_B2(f_n)=omega(n): for every c>0 there is N such that C_B2(f_n)>c*n for every n>=N. The circuits have unrestricted depth and fan-out; no fixed linear constant counts as superlinear.

Source: [3.1n - o(n) Circuit Lower Bounds for Explicit Functions, ECCC TR21-023,20February2021](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2021/023/download/).

title: Capacity of the Binary Deletion Channel
statement:
Determine the exact average-error Shannon capacity C_del(d), in bits per input bit, of the binary deletion channel for every real d with 0<d<1. Each input bit is independently deleted with probability d; surviving bits retain their order, and neither terminal observes the deletion pattern.

Source: [Cheraghchi and Ribeiro, An Overview of Capacity Results for Synchronization Channels](https://arxiv.org/html/1910.07199v2).

title: Global Regularity of the 2D Inviscid Boussinesq Equations
statement:
Determine whether all smooth, finite-energy solutions of the two-dimensional inviscid Boussinesq equations (velocity coupled to a temperature or density by buoyancy, without dissipation) on R^2 remain smooth for all time, or whether finite-time singularity formation occurs for some C^infinity initial data; finite-time blow-up is known for some data on domains with corners and near half-space type domains.

Source: [Kyungkeun Kang, Jihoon Lee, and Dinh Duong Nguyen, Global well-posedness and stability of the 2D Boussinesq equations with partial dissipation (2024), Section 1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.08286).
